cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has had hard news for God's people. They ran to Egypt for help without asking the LORD, and when He told them repentance and rest would save them, they said no thanks, we'll flee on horses (Isaiah 30:2, 15-16). So when the prophet says "Therefore," friend, I'd be hiding behind my own mustache.

cards.question: After all that running and refusing, the prophet says "Therefore." What does the LORD long to do for His people?

cards.text: He rises to show them compassion. Then the prophet says, "Blessed are all who wait for Him." Friend, waiting is NOT my gift. I stare at that oven light like it owes me money.

cards.question: The prophet says the LORD rises to show His people compassion because He is a just God.

cards.text: Then the prophet speaks straight to the people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem: "you will weep no more." No more weeping? Friend, I tear up when the oven timer goes off ON TIME. That's a BIG promise.

cards.question: When the people in Jerusalem cry for help, the LORD hears them but stays silent.

cards.text: Now, hard days still come: the Lord will give them the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. That's one delivery NOBODY tips the driver for.

cards.question: Even in those hard days, something changes about the people's Teacher. What is it?

answers.text: He will no longer hide Himself
He will leave them on their own
He will only speak in dreams

cards.text: With their own eyes they'll see Him. And whether they turn to the right or to the left, their ears will hear a command behind them.

cards.question: Whether they turn right or left, the command behind them tells God's people which ___ to walk in.

cards.text: And the command is, "This is the way. Walk in it." A voice that steers you right BEFORE you're three exits past it? Friend, that beats every map app on earth.

cards.question: Now God's people are walking His way. What do they do with their silver-plated idols and gold-plated images?

cards.text: They desecrate those idols, toss them out and tell them, "Be gone!" Then the prophet turns to the seed they've sown in the ground.

cards.question: The LORD will send ___ for the seed they have sown in the ground.
Even after the LORD sends rain for their seed, the food from their land stays thin and scarce.

cards.text: Their cattle graze in open pastures, and the oxen and donkeys eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork. Friend, those donkeys are eating fancier than I ever did in the drawer, and I lived on DUST.

cards.question: There's water coming too. Where will streams of water flow from?

answers.text: Every high mountain and raised hill

cards.text: Those streams flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall. Then the sky joins in: the moon as bright as the sun, and the sun SEVEN times brighter.

cards.question: The moon shines like the sun, and the sun shines seven times brighter. On what day does that happen?

answers.text: When the LORD heals His people
When Egypt's army arrives to help
When Jerusalem's new wall is done

cards.text: That's the day the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted. The same hand that struck them is the hand that heals them.
Then the prophet says, "Behold," and the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.

cards.question: The LORD comes to sift His own people in a sieve of destruction.

cards.text: It's the nations He sifts, and His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray, like a horse with a bit that does NOT get to pick the road.

cards.question: Then the prophet turns back to God's people. What will they do?

answers.text: Sing as on a festival night

cards.text: Their hearts will rejoice like someone walking to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel. Picture your best commute ever, then delete the traffic.

cards.question: The LORD will make His majestic voice heard and reveal His mighty arm, striking in angry wrath. What comes with it?

cards.text: Then the prophet names a nation: Assyria, the empire God once called the rod of His anger (Isaiah 10:5). At the voice of the LORD, Assyria will be shattered.

cards.question: At the voice of the LORD, Assyria is shattered, and He strikes them with His ___.

cards.text: The LORD brings down His rod of punishment on them, stroke after stroke, as He battles with weapons brandished.

cards.question: With every stroke of the LORD's rod on Assyria, tambourines and lyres will sound.

cards.text: Then the prophet names a place: Topheth. It has long been prepared, made ready for the king, and its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood.

cards.question: Topheth's pyre is ready for the king. What sets it ablaze, like a torrent of burning sulfur?

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'He rises to show them compassion.' / 'Then the prophet says, "Blessed are all who wait for Him."' / 'Friend, waiting is NOT my gift.' / 'I stare at that oven light like it owes me money.' It is not the opening card, so the limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: the line to the people in Zion, 'No more weeping?', the oven timer joke, and 'That's a BIG promise.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks for 'way', the key word of the command 'This is the way. Walk in it.' (Isaiah 30:21). The baker hasn't seen that command yet, so the blank tests unseen wording. 'Which ___ to walk in' also completes to the everyday phrase 'which way to walk', so the right answer stands out. 'City' and 'field' don't fit the sentence naturally.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'City' and 'field' don't read naturally in 'which ___ to walk in', so 'way' stands out from the other answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the sentence quoting the command, the map-app question, and 'Friend, that beats every map app on earth.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank finishes the line 'He will strike them with His scepter' (Isaiah 30:31). The baker can't reason out scepter over sling or spear from earlier cards, so this is guessing the next word of a line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question: what sets Topheth ablaze. The wrong answers 'A torch from the king' and 'A spark from Jerusalem' are made-up details, not real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
